parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two identical oil droplets are in a vacuum. The centres of the droplets are a distance of $3.8 \times 10^{-6} \text{m}$ apart. The droplets have equal charge and exert an electric force on each other of magnitude $6.3 \times 10^{-17} \text{N}$.

Determine the magnitude of the charge on each droplet.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem:
One of the oil droplets in (b) is now placed between two horizontal metal plates, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1}}

Fig. 5.1 (not to scale)

A potential difference (p.d.) of $1200 \text{V}$ is applied between the plates, with the top plate at the higher potential. The oil droplet is stationary and in equilibrium.
parts.text: State the sign of the charge on the oil droplet.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw four lines to represent the electric field between the plates.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The distance between the plates is $5.2 \text{cm}$.

Determine the mass of the oil droplet.
